/look_brief.audience: the public who fund and use the parks: visitors, neighbours of the parks, schools, local journalists and elected members' staff, none of whom commissioned the report or know its terms
/look_brief.occasion: a five-page section of the annual report, published as a PDF read on laptops and phones at the reader's own pace and printed for libraries and visitor centres; nobody presents it, so every chart must read without a speaker
/look_brief.subject_world: parks live by waymarked trails and the topographic map: a numbered waymark post tells a walker where they are on a route, and a map legend keys a small swatch to a plain word. The section borrows both conventions: a numbered waymark disc beside each title marks the five sections in order, and series are named by words in their own colour on the marks, like a map key, instead of a boxed legend. It leaves out contour textures, wood-grain signs, leaf icons, mountain silhouettes and the black band of a real park agency's publications: none has a job on a data page, and the last would pass as another agency's trade dress
/look_brief.data_character: modest and mixed: one twelve-month series in two years, two shares, a nine-row ranking of signed changes, a budget of five income lines and six spending lines that must tie, a five-year series with a count under each year, and a five-row table of commitments; one or two exhibits a page, each with a sentence or two of plain explanation

density.target: one main exhibit per page with at most one supporting exhibit or a short text column; 90 to 150 words a page; tables of five or six rows
density.why: a general reader skims the title, looks at one picture and reads two sentences; more exhibits per page would ask them to do the comparison work a banker does, and the figures they need are few

/look_brief.look: an outdoor, plain-spoken report: warm paper-white pages, sentence titles in a bookish serif (Georgia) over Arial for every figure, a deep lake blue for this year's figures, stone grey for last year, and one sunset orange that points at the figure the title states

colour_meanings.color.accent1: this year's figures and the structure that carries them: the current series, the waymark discs, the rule under a table header
colour_meanings.color.accent3: last year or a baseline, set back behind this year's figures
colour_meanings.color.emphasis: look here: the single place on an exhibit where the title's claim lands (a peak, a share, a ring), labelled in words
colour_meanings.color.accent2: the same sunset orange as emphasis, used as a fill when the look-here mark is a bar or a segment
colour_meanings.color.positive: a population that grew since the baseline, only on the conservation page
colour_meanings.color.negative: a population that fell since the baseline, only on the conservation page
colour_meanings.color.surface_alt: a panel that holds side facts apart from the main exhibit

/look_brief.type_ladder: built from the densest page, the priorities table, whose cells hold short sentences in four columns: 10.5pt Arial cells stay readable on a phone screen zoomed to the page and in print; axis labels 10pt and data labels 10.5pt bold so values read before marks; footnotes and sources 8.5pt, above the 7pt floor; body 12pt for the explanation a general reader actually reads; panel headings 15pt Georgia; titles 24pt Georgia bold to carry a plain claim on at most two lines

rejected.what: forest green and brown as the main pair
rejected.why: it is the costume of park agencies and green would then mean both 'our figures' and 'a species growing'; lake blue leads so green can mean growth only

rejected.what: a doughnut for where the money goes
rejected.why: six slices of 3 to 32 percent cannot be compared by angle; sorted bars with 'of every $100' labels read as plain counts

rejected.what: icons for each spending area and activity
rejected.why: a tent or a leaf adds no fact to a labelled bar and competes with the figure

rejected.what: big standalone numbers for the headlines
rejected.why: a figure without last year beside it tells a general reader nothing about whether it is good; each headline sits with its comparison
every mark carries its value and each series is named on the chart in its own colour

/description.summary: An outdoor, plain-spoken public report: warm paper-white pages, sentence titles in Georgia beside a numbered waymark disc, Arial for every figure, lake blue for this year, stone grey for last, sunset orange for the one place to look.
/description.typography: Georgia bold titles at 24pt and panel heads at 15pt; Arial body at 12pt, table cells 10.5pt, labels 10 to 10.5pt, notes 8.5pt.
/description.color: Lake blue leads, stone grey recedes, sunset orange points; green and red only for species that grew or fell.
/description.layout: 0.6in side margins, a title row with a waymark disc, one main exhibit and at most one supporting block, a hairline footer with the report's name.
/description.tables: No fills; bold header over a lake-blue rule, hairline rows, totals bold over a rule.
/description.motifs: the numbered waymark disc beside each title

/continuation.why: a page that splits repeats its title with (continued) after it
